question.text: Which of the following is a key feature of a floating rate bond?

answer.text: It pays a fixed coupon throughout its life
It is always issued at a discount to face value
It does not pay any coupon and returns only the face value at maturity
Its interest rate/coupon is reset periodically with reference to a benchmark rate such as the RBI Repo Rate

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series II-A (p.35), a floating rate bond is one whose interest rate/coupon is reset periodically with reference to a benchmark rate such as the RBI Repo Rate; such bonds are also called variable or adjustable rate bonds. The Trap: Option A describes a fixed-rate (plain vanilla) bond; option C describes a zero-coupon bond — both contrasts are drawn out on p.34. Option B is not a defining feature of any specific bond type. Note: The benchmark-linked periodic reset is the defining characteristic the source uses to identify floating rate bonds.
